title: The Kan extension preserves distinguished source triangles
statement: Let $D,D^{\prime}$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] and let $L$ be a category with coherent integer shifts. Let $F:D\to D^{\prime}$ be exact and let $S$ be a saturated triangulated multiplicative system [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. Let $Q:D\to L$ be a shift-compatible localization of $D$ at $S$. Let $LF:L\to D^{\prime}$ have coherent integer-shift comparisons and let $\alpha:Q\circ LF\to F$ exhibit a right Kan extension and commute with shifts. If the denominator pro-diagram of $F$ at every object of $D$ is essentially constant, then for every distinguished triangle $T$ of $D$, the triangle $(Q\circ LF)(T)$ is distinguished in $D^{\prime}$.

proof.text: For each X, unpack a witnessing denominator value and apply leftDerived_defined_pointwiseKan_bridge. This gives HasPointwiseRightKanExtensionAt at Q(X). Essential surjectivity of Q and invariance of pointwise existence under object isomorphisms give HasPointwiseRightKanExtension everywhere.

Apply leftDerived_map_distinguished_of_two_defined to T, using the first two supplied instances of definedness. Unpack its three values, witnessing cones, maps, denominator equations, and distinguishedness conclusion.

Apply leftDerived_kan_triangle_value_comparison to this data. It identifies the image triangle with the distinguished value triangle. Closure under triangle isomorphism proves distinguishedness of the image.
